text: The patient was admitted with fever, productive cough, and shortness of breath. Chest examination suggested lower respiratory tract infection. Intravenous antibiotics and oxygen were started. Over two days, breathing improved and fever settled. The patient was discharged with oral antibiotics and follow-up advice.
summary: The patient was treated for a lower respiratory infection with antibiotics and oxygen. Symptoms improved, and discharge follow-up was advised.

text: A 58-year-old patient with hypertension reported chest pain and dizziness. Initial blood pressure was markedly elevated. ECG did not show acute myocardial infarction. Antihypertensive treatment was adjusted and pain improved with monitoring. The patient was discharged in stable condition with advice to continue medicines and review blood pressure control.
summary: The report describes uncontrolled hypertension with chest pain but no acute heart attack on ECG. Treatment was adjusted, symptoms improved, and blood pressure follow-up was recommended.

text: The report notes uncontrolled blood sugar with fatigue and increased urination. HbA1c was elevated, supporting poorly controlled diabetes. Diet counseling and medication review were provided. The patient was advised to monitor blood sugar regularly and return for follow-up.
summary: The patient has poorly controlled diabetes based on elevated HbA1c. Counseling, medication review, and regular blood sugar follow-up were advised.
